title: Areas Between Curves
summary: The area between two curves is $\int_a^b(\text{top}-\text{bottom})\,dx$. Find the bounds from intersection points, integrate the height difference, and switch to $\int(\text{right}-\text{left})\,dy$ when horizontal strips are simpler.

area between curves.plain: The region trapped between two graphs.

top minus bottom.plain: The height of a vertical strip.
top minus bottom.in_class: Upper curve value minus lower curve value.

intersection points.plain: Where the curves meet, setting the bounds.

which is on top.plain: The larger function over the interval.
which is on top.in_class: Test a sample point if unsure.

signed vs geometric area.in_class: Different from a single signed integral.

split the region.plain: Break where the curves swap order.
split the region.in_class: Integrate each piece with the correct top.

concept_sections.heading: The height-difference integral
concept_sections.explanation: Between $x=a$ and $x=b$, a vertical strip has height (top curve $-$ bottom curve). Integrating this height gives the area: $\int_a^b (f-g)\,dx$.
math_steps: Identify the upper and lower curves.

concept_sections.heading: Finding the bounds
concept_sections.explanation: The limits come from where the curves cross. Solve $f(x)=g(x)$ for the intersection $x$-values; those are $a$ and $b$.
math_steps: Use the smallest and largest as bounds.

concept_sections.heading: Deciding which is on top
concept_sections.explanation: Over the interval, one curve stays above. Test a sample $x$ between the intersections to see which value is larger, and put it first.
math_steps: Pick a test point between crossings.

concept_sections.heading: Horizontal strips
concept_sections.explanation: When curves are easier as $x=$ functions of $y$ (sideways parabolas, etc.), integrate right$-$left in $y$: $\int_c^d(\text{right}-\text{left})\,dy$.

concept_sections.heading: Regions that swap
concept_sections.explanation: If the curves cross inside the interval, the top and bottom trade places. Split at the crossing and integrate each piece with its correct height.

real_world_examples.title: Profit between revenue and cost
real_world_examples.scenario: Revenue and cost curves versus quantity.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The area between them over the profitable range represents total profit.

real_world_examples.title: Cross-section of a lens
real_world_examples.scenario: A lens bounded by two arcs.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The area between the arcs gives the lens's cross-sectional area.

real_world_examples.title: Water between two levels
real_world_examples.scenario: A channel bounded above and below by curves.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The between-curves integral gives the cross-sectional flow area.
